content.text:
I'm not going to fix this one, Rajat.

I looked at the repo. It's Natively, and its README sells it as an "undetectable interview AI", "HackerRank AI cheat" and "hidden interview tool". The overlay being invisible to screen share is the part that keeps the other person from seeing it. You're in the middle of recruiting, so the most likely use is having AI help on screen during an interview or assessment without the interviewer knowing. I won't make that concealment work. If you were caught, it could also cost you offers, which matters more on F-1 with a December graduation.

On why it's showing up: it's probably not a bug in your copy. Recent macOS versions capture through ScreenCaptureKit, and Zoom, Meet and Teams have moved to it. That capture path ignores the window exclusion flag these apps depend on, so the "stealth" overlay is visible on a lot of current setups no matter what the code does.

If you have a different use in mind, tell me. For example, private notes during your own demo work fine as a second-monitor window or a phone. I'm also happy to help with other parts of this app, or with interview prep: mock coding rounds, system design practice, or going through problems you've struggled with.
